context:
This is a decision item, not an implementation item. Produce a number, then decide a cap.

DECISION GATE w2: choose ONE policy and record it: (a) a hard ratio cap -- process churn may not exceed product churn over a rolling window; (b) a freeze list of paths that accept only defect fixes until a named customer-facing milestone ships; (c) no cap, with the reason recorded and this item dropped. Option (c) is a legitimate outcome if the measurement does not hold up; what is not acceptable is leaving it unexamined.

Whichever is chosen, keep every safety gate. The target is discretionary process ENGINEERING -- new tracker features, new agent instruction surfaces, new meta-tests -- not the checks that protect releases and privacy.
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 over git history since 2026-06-01 (991 commits on the local develop tip).

CORRECTION FIRST: an earlier pass of this review reported '714 of 991 commits (72%) touched only process files'. That figure was WRONG -- the classifier used 'grep -qv', and this machine's grep is ugrep, where -q reports whether any line MATCHED and ignores the -v inversion, so every commit containing any process path was scored process-only. Two independent adversarial reviewers flagged it. Do not cite the 72% figure.

The corrected, reproducible measurements:
 - Commits touching ONLY process paths (_project/, .github/, docs/operations/, docs/agent/, .claude/, .todo*, scripts/, make/, Makefile, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md): 208 of 991 (21%). An independent reviewer got ~200 by the same definition.
 - Commits touching the shipped package benchbox/: 373 of 991 (37.6%).
 - Line churn, excluding the bulk results-data/ JSON which would otherwise dominate: agent and tracker process files 389,833 lines (60.7%); the shipped Python package 65,051 lines (10.1%); process-scaffolding tests 57,286 lines (8.9%); the results explorer 6,038 lines (0.9%); user docs 4,226 lines (0.7%).
 - Standing surface: 31 CI workflows; 151 targets in the Makefile (191 tracked in make/inventory.json); a 1,796-line Makefile plus 584 lines across make/*.mk; 133 of 1,343 test_*.py files (9.9%) test process scaffolding rather than the product.

So the commit-count story is unremarkable and the CHURN story is the real one: roughly six lines of hand-written change go into tracker and agent-process files for every one that goes into the thing customers install.

Secondary evidence of the cost: _project/todo-db-export/ was last written 2026-08-16 and already disagrees with the live tracker -- during this review an external reviewer drew four wrong conclusions from it, including claims about items that had been revalidated on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-20. A published artifact that is a week stale is worse than no artifact.

This item is deliberately NOT 'delete the gates'. Adversarial review pushed back on that and was right: the UAT, privacy and release-evidence gates exist because v0.3.0 shipped a broken install.

anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD use 21% of commits and the 60.7%/10.1% churn split
anti_patterns.why: it was an artifact of ugrep's -qv semantics and is wrong

anti_patterns.dont: Delete or disable the UAT, privacy, submission or release-evidence gates under this item
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD target only discretionary process engineering
anti_patterns.why: they exist because v0.3.0 shipped a broken install, and adversarial review specifically rejected removing them

anti_patterns.dont: Implement a blocking CI gate that fails builds on a churn ratio
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD make it an observable report
anti_patterns.why: that adds process to solve a process problem

anti_patterns.dont: Treat this item as authorization to stop tracker work mid-flight
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD apply the decision to new discretionary work
anti_patterns.why: in-flight items still need their evidence recorded

preserves.behavior: Every existing safety gate stays: UAT release-gate evidence, corpus privacy scrubbing, submission validation, release rollback targets
Worktree write policy, commit identity policy, and the no-agent-attribution rule are unaffected

prior_art.concept: existing shrink program and its ledger

verifications.command: run the w0 script against git history since 2026-06-01
verifications.expected: process-to-product churn ratio is reported and matches the recorded figure within rounding
w2 evidence names the chosen option and the reason

work_units.summary: Re-derive every figure in the description with a checked-in script; do not reuse the numbers quoted here without reproducing them
Separate discretionary process engineering from safety gates, naming which paths fall in each
DECISION GATE - choose ratio cap, freeze list, or no cap; record the reason
Decide whether _project/todo-db-export/ should be refreshed on a schedule, marked clearly as a dated snapshot, or withdrawn, given it misled an external reviewer while a week stale
If a cap or freeze is chosen, make it observable - a periodic report, not a blocking gate
